about.title: Del Rey Oaks Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Del Rey Oaks is a small city, but its workers still face the same on-the-job risks found anywhere in Monterey County — falls, equipment accidents, vehicle collisions while making deliveries along Rt 68 or Canyon Del Rey Boulevard, and repetitive strain from physical labor. Most of the time, a workplace injury here is handled through California workers' compensation, which pays medical care and partial wage replacement no matter who caused the accident. But comp isn't the whole story. If a subcontractor, property owner, delivery vehicle, or piece of equipment made by someone other than your employer contributed to your injury, you may also have a separate claim against that third party. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we connect injured workers in Del Rey Oaks with an independent attorney, free of charge, who can look at both sides of your situation: the workers' comp claim and any potential third-party case, so nothing gets left on the table.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Del Rey Oaks Workplace Injury

items.title: Comp Isn't Always the Only Path
items.desc: California workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker can still be held liable in a separate claim.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and missing that window can complicate your comp claim, so early legal guidance helps protect your rights.

items.title: Retaliation Is Against the Law
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from punishing workers for reporting an injury or filing a claim, and an attorney can help you understand your protections if you're worried about your job.

items.question: I was hurt on a job site near Rt 218 in Del Rey Oaks — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, you'll start with a workers' compensation claim through your employer, since that's usually the exclusive remedy regardless of fault. However, if someone other than your employer, like a contractor or equipment supplier, contributed to the accident, you may also have a separate third-party claim. An independent attorney can review the details and explain which paths apply to your situation.

items.question: What if my employer tries to punish me for reporting my injury?
items.answer: California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting a workplace injury or filing a workers' comp claim. If you experience pushback, reduced hours, or termination connected to your report, an attorney can help you understand your options. Documenting what happens is helpful if you decide to pursue this further.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a third-party claim after a work injury in Del Rey Oaks?
items.answer: Third-party injury claims in California generally carry a two-year deadline from the date of the injury. This is separate from the workers' comp reporting window, which is typically 30 days from the incident. Because these timelines don't always align, it's worth getting a free case review sooner rather than later.
